title: Last Moment Before All Ants Fall Out of a Plank
spaceBreakdown:
- local int ans: O(1)
- no containers, no recursion
- not counted: input vectors left, right
approach: When two ants collide and reverse direction, the set of positions occupied by ants is identical to what it would be if they simply passed through each other (the ants are indistinguishable). So we can ignore collisions entirely: each left-moving ant at position x falls at time x, and each right-moving ant at position x falls at time n−x. The answer is the maximum of these times over all ants.
hints: When two ants meet head-on and both reverse, how does the resulting set of occupied positions compare to the case where they had simply walked through each other?

Use the collision-equivalence trick: treat every ant as moving straight to its target end. For Example 1 (n=4, left=[4,3], right=[0,1]): left ant at 4 takes 4s, right ant at 0 takes 4−0=4s → answer 4.

```
ans = 0
for x in left:
    ans = max(ans, x)
for x in right:
    ans = max(ans, n - x)
return ans
```

**Empty left array** - only right-moving ants exist.
`Input: n = 7, left = [], right = [0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7]` → `Expected: 7`
⚠️ Bug: calling `*max_element(left.begin(), left.end())` on an empty vector → undefined behavior / crash.

**Empty right array** - only left-moving ants exist.
`Input: n = 7, left = [0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7], right = []` → `Expected: 7`
⚠️ Bug: calling `*max_element(right.begin(), right.end())` on an empty vector → undefined behavior / crash.

**Single ant at position 0 going right** - minimal right input.
`Input: n = 5, left = [], right = [0]` → `Expected: 5`
⚠️ Bug: initializing `ans = left[0]` without checking left is empty → undefined behavior / crash.

**Ant already at the far end** - left ant at position n.
`Input: n = 5, left = [5], right = []` → `Expected: 5`
⚠️ Bug: computing `n - x` for left-moving ants instead of `x` → returns 0.

followUps.q: What if each ant has a different integer speed instead of speed 1?
followUps.a: The collision-equivalence trick still holds for positions (ants are indistinguishable), but the fall time of an ant starting at x with speed v going right is (n−x)/v and going left is x/v. Take the max over all ants. Time O(L+R), space O(1).

followUps.q: What if n can be up to 10^9 - does the algorithm change?
followUps.a: No. We never allocate an array of size n; we only iterate the two input lists, so the same O(L+R) time, O(1) space solution works unchanged.

followUps.q: What if you must also return the total number of ant-ant collisions before all fall?
followUps.a: Under the pass-through model, a left ant at position a and a right ant at position b with a > b will meet exactly once. So count pairs (a in left, b in right) with a > b; sort right and binary-search, or sort both and two-pointer. Time O(L log L + R log R), space O(1) extra (in-place sort).
